newsitem.title: FRANCE: Monod wants 2-tier board in Suez/Lyonnaise merger.
newsitem.headline: Monod wants 2-tier board in Suez/Lyonnaise merger.

text.p: Lyonnaise des Eaux chairman Jerome Monod said in a newspaper interview published on Tuesday that he hoped a merger deal with Suez would be wrapped up on Friday to create a global player called Suez-Lyonnaise des Eaux.
He said that, contrary to press speculation, he wanted the group to be run by a supervisory board in charge of strategy and an executive board headed by Suez chairman Gerard Mestrallet.
"We have to rise up to the challenge of a new strategy with global ambitions, of running a new company, Suez-Lyonnaise des Eaux, as that will be it offical name...," Monod told Le Figaro.
The firms have already accepted the principle of merging.
Monod told the daily newspaper he hoped the two firms would quickly meet the challenge in a global market where the large players were operational groups rather than holding companies.
"The big global groups are operations-based ones, focused on a few areas, rather than companies of industrial holdings," he was quoted as saying. "France is behind the times on this."
On the merger, Monod said: "The new group will have 200 billion francs in sales after the merger, employing 190,000."
This, he said, had required serious reflection on how to manage the group into the 21st century. "I have therefore chosen the formula of a supervisory and executive board," he said.
He said the executive board would deal with operational issues and the supervisory board with strategy.

"I am convinced this is the most appropriate formula for the long-term success of this merger," he said. "This decision will take immediate effect from June 1997, before the normal expiry date of my manadate at Lyonnaise, which is September 1998."

Monod did not make it clear what precisely his own position would be. "Regarding myself, it's not a departure, it's a change. I will take take charge, for as long as is necessary, of seeing Suez-Lyonnaise enter the 21st century.

"I want the merger to be decided on Friday," he said, adding that he would work with Gerard Mestrallet "as future head of the executive board" on getting the merger prepared for the annual shareholder meetings in June.

Monod said nothing of the terms on which the merger was likely to be undertaken. Newspapers believe the transaction could be carried on a ratio of 41 Suez shares for 20 Lyonnaise, accompanied by a special payout from Suez to sweeten the deal for Suez shareholders.
Some of those same media reports, however, said the merged group was expected to have a single board headed by Monod.
